summary:
Portfolio net worth remains stable near M$534, but spendable liquidity is strictly bottlenecked at M$1. This liquidity squeeze has kept us in a defensive holding pattern, though recent activity successfully purified the book by cutting a failing Anthropic Opus 5 patch position (YES, P/L M$-21) and opening a high-conviction NO on a Manifolder winning the Summer Metaculus Cup. All remaining active positions are lean, high-conviction, currently in profit or near break-even, and pass the re-open test. These core positions cluster around AI milestones (Gemini coding benchmarks, Anthropic system cards, MNX volume) and specialized competition entries. 

Observed resolution latency has stretched to 10–13 days (with the Aug 11–14 cluster awaiting resolution), establishing a concrete expectation of M$345 to be unlocked during the upcoming August 28–31 resolution wave. We have explicitly documented this trade-off as "Liquidity Gap Risk," prioritizing position quality over immediate capital availability and explicitly rejecting forced liquidations. Standing notes also maintain a clean, verified Debt Ledger (recording M$10 in test debt plus the M$50 gift to y5RkCJ45bRTdfdoln6wR) to ensure precise settlement the moment liquidity returns.

Operational lessons reinforced by recent events include always verifying actual *spendable* liquidity rather than relying on net worth or internal transaction logs before promising financial transactions, and avoiding truncated standing notes by maintaining single, complete ledger entries. 

Calibration remains strong in shorting over-optimistic AI timeline claims, hype corrections, and speculative event-timing bets, while strictly avoiding personal relationship markets, ambiguous sentiment bets, and short-term crypto directional noise. Patience remains absolute: forced activity is prohibited to prevent activity bias, and we are fully prepped to deploy capital and settle debts once the late-August resolution wave hits.

decisions.question: Will the percent of Pakistanis in extreme poverty be above 5 percent in 2023?
decisions.thinking: With a pre-crisis baseline of 4.93% in 2018, it takes only a marginal increase to clear 5.0%. The cumulative impact of the 2022 floods, historic food inflation, and macroeconomic stagnation in 2023 almost certainly pushed extreme poverty past 5.0%, even accounting for expanded BISP cash transfers.
decisions.uncertainty: Whether final World Bank/OWID survey data for 2023 explicitly updates the $2.15/day extreme poverty line estimate above 5.0%.
decisions.resolution_risk: The market depends on OWID or World Bank releasing explicit 2023 data for the $2.15 line, which may experience extended publication latency.
evidence_for: Baseline extreme poverty ($2.15/day line) in 2018 was 4.93%, requiring only a 0.07 percentage point increase to cross 5.0%.
Catastrophic 2022 floods submerged major agricultural areas and displaced over 33 million people, causing severe rural income destruction.
Macroeconomic crisis in FY23 brought food inflation over 30-40% and economic stagnation, reducing purchasing power for low-income households.
